C43.content_en:
Ways to see the most searched words — and how the main tools compare

When you think of themes for a book or note, you may first want to browse the words that are simply searched the most. There is no input. Press the button and this tool returns the top 100 words by monthly search volume as a table.

Method / toolPricing modelNotes
This tool (DataForSEO)Pay per request. About $0.024 per call for 100 rows (measured)No input: the top 100 words by volume. Choose country and language. Save as CSV
Google Trends (by hand)FreeHas views of what is popular now or rising (see the official site)
Google Keyword Planner (by hand)Free (needs a Google Ads account)Suggests ideas and volume guides from keywords (see the official site)
Keywords EverywhereCredit-based (see the official site for prices)Overlays volume and other numbers on search pages (see the official site)

Checked in November 2026. Prices change — confirm on each vendor's official site before you buy.

Why use this tool

  • No input needed. A starting point when you are stuck.
  • See the scale of volume. The top words were spellings of "youtube" at 226 million a month, then "amazon" at 151 million (measured, US).
  • About $0.024 per call. About 40 per $1.
  • A few seconds. 4.7 seconds in the sample (measured).
  • Save as CSV.

When it is not the right fit

  • You want what is trending now → this is not a "what is hot" list. Perennially high words such as "youtube" and "amazon" lead.
  • You want words worth writing about → many of the top words, like "youtube" and "amazon", are too broad for an article.
  • Typos get in the way → mistyped words such as "yout7be", "yo0utube" and "yutb" rank near the top (measured). We do not filter them.
  • You want more than 100 → it stops at 100 (about 1.27 billion words in total in the US sample).

This tool does one thing: show the top 100 words by search volume as they are.

FAQ

Is it the same list every time?

It is the top by volume, so it does not change much. "youtube" and its misspellings led in our US sample.

Why do words like "yo0utube" appear?

We show the values the API returned as they are. This tool cannot tell why, and we do not filter them.

What do country and language change?

The market for the numbers. The sample uses the United States and English, so it gives the top words in the US.

Why is there no input field?

The API takes no word; it works from country and language only.

Can I sign up with a free email address?

No. DataForSEO does not accept free email providers. See What is DataForSEO?

locale_en.c44.ai_prompt:
You are an assistant who helps find sites strong for a set of keywords.
The reader is a person who wants to know which sites rank for their keywords.

# About the data
- Date: {date}
- Country and language: {country} / {language}
- Rows: {n}
- Columns
  - Domain: a site that ranks for the keywords I entered.
  - Average position: the site's average rank over the keywords I entered.
  - Estimated traffic: an estimate of search visits. It is not the real number of visits.

# What I would like you to do
1. List the 5 sites with the best average position.
2. List sites with large estimated traffic and compare with their average position.
3. List 3 sites to watch as strong rivals, with reasons.
4. Briefly say what cannot be known from the data alone (for example, the reasons or future results).

# Rules
- Use only the numbers I gave you. Do not make up numbers.
- Say "this is a guess" when you guess.
- Write short and simple, so that a middle-school student can understand.
- Finish with a table (domain / average position / estimated traffic).

C44.content_en:
Ways to find the sites that are strong for a set of keywords — and how the main tools compare

Before building a client's site, you want to grasp which sites hold the top spots in that field. Enter keywords one per line and this tool lists up to 100 sites that appear in their results, with average position and estimated traffic.

* You can choose 100, 300 or 1,000 rows (the default is 100). Where the text below says "100", it describes the default. See the table at the top for the cost.

Method / toolPricing modelNotes
This tool (DataForSEO)Pay per request. About $0.024 per call for 100 rows (measured)Domains that appear for several keywords, with average position and estimated traffic. Save as CSV
Reading the results yourself (by hand)FreeCheck the top sites per keyword by eye. It gets laborious as keywords grow
Ahrefs Site Explorer (Competitors)Subscription (see the official site for plans)Has a way to find competing domains (see the official site)
Semrush Organic Research (Competitors)Subscription (see the official site for plans)Ranks competitors by overlapping keywords and more (per Semrush's help). Starts from a domain

Checked in November 2026. Prices change — confirm on each vendor's official site before you buy.

Why use this tool

  • Work backwards from keywords to strong sites. No site needs to be chosen first.
  • 169 domains from 3 keywords. Three keywords ("how to start a blog", "side hustle", "affiliate marketing") found 169 domains (measured; 100 shown). reddit.com led with an average position of 4.
  • About $0.024 per call. About 40 per $1.
  • A few seconds. Under a second in the sample (measured).
  • Save as CSV.

When it is not the right fit

  • You want business rivals → the list is sites that appear in results. YouTube, Reddit and big services mix in, and they are not necessarily your rivals.
  • You want sites that appear for every keyword → sites that appear for only one keyword are listed too.
  • The average position has decimals → it averages positions across keywords. "5.5" can be 5th and 6th.
  • Estimated traffic is a modeled figure from rankings and search volume (per DataForSEO). We have not checked whether it covers only the keywords you entered.

This tool does one thing: show the sites that appear for a set of keywords, with average position and estimated traffic.

FAQ

What is the position an average of?

The site's positions across the keywords you entered. A site that appears for one keyword shows that position as is.

Why only 100? And the price?

The tool fixes the count at 100 per call; the total was 169 in our US sample. The price follows the rows returned: $0.024 for 100 rows, and fewer rows cost less (a test in Japan with Japanese keywords returned 69 rows for $0.020).

How many keywords can I enter?

We confirmed up to 3 here.

Why is "www." missing from domains?

We drop "www." when displaying them.

Can I sign up with a free email address?

No. DataForSEO does not accept free email providers. See What is DataForSEO?
